designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Tight 4x5 grid with even rhythm, consistent rounded-stroke icons and a condensed-caps label system that reads like a real manual; the heavy grotesque PROBABLY FINE. spans the grid width exactly and lands the joke with the right deadpan weight. Reads as a clear block from 3 m and rewards a close look. Minor: the ABS glyph uses a different (lighter, wider) face than everything else, and the labels sit a touch far below their icons, loosening the cells.
designs.fix: Tighten the icon-to-label gap and re-draw the ABS lettering in the same condensed stroke weight so the grid reads as one family; give the headline slightly more air above it than between grid rows so it separates as the punchline.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Elegant pairing: letterspaced roman caps title, small moon as a pivot, italic serif captions, loose brush dogs; the 2-column grid resolving to a single centred step 7 gives the sequence a natural ending. The repeated 'Turn around.' does the comic work through typography alone. Weak points: the turning poses are not clearly progressive, so the rotation gag reads a little random, and captions get small and thin on the tee at chest scale.
designs.fix: Redraw steps 2-5 as a clear progressive rotation (dog visibly turning a quarter more each step, tightening into the curl of step 6) and bump caption size about 15% so the italic survives the knit.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Clean, confident line work and nice frame-breaks (cat's tail, the rejected bed spilling out of panel 3), but the composition is lopsided: numbers float in a wide empty left gutter so the stack sits off-centre on the tee, the three equal panels give no emphasis to the payoff, and with no type at all it reads as an instruction leaflet rather than a designed piece. The cat-in-box joke is familiar and needs sharper staging to carry $50.
designs.fix: Pull the numerals into the panel corners (or tuck them tight to the frames) and centre the stack on the garment, then make panel 3 noticeably larger than 1 and 2 so the punchline gets the visual weight.
